editorial: You’re drawn into a late‑90s high‑school frame that feels like a secretive sliver of collective memory, where the janitor’s fluorescent strip acts as a prelude to something otherworldly. The film’s restrained, slow‑burn pacing makes the ordinary feel uncanny, turning every hallway echo into a hint of the unseen broadcast. Its most arresting moment lies in a tense dreamlike montage where the late‑night TV seems to pull a live feed from your own personal world. If you thrive on films that make you question what you think is real, this supernatural thriller will keep you glowing with anticipation. The tone is cerebral and visually intense, marrying nostalgia with a quietly invasive dread that permeates each frame.
targetAudience: Ideal for fans of psychological thrillers who enjoy non-linear storytelling.
